result.title: SKALOS: Learning to Distinguish Similar Skills with Capability Graphs
result.summary: Skills provide LLM agents with reusable procedural knowledge, making appropriate skill selection essential for reliable agent behavior. As skill libraries expand, distinguishing semantically similar candidates becomes increasingly difficult. Existing methods encode or rewrite skill descriptions for relevance-based ranking, yet heterogeneous descriptions can obscure capability differences. To address this challenge, we propose SKALOS, a graph-native reranker that compares skills via explicit capability evidence. Its multi-hierarchy graph aligns equivalent expressions across skills while preserving skill-specific capability evidence. Since individually relevant capability elements may not jointly support a query, semiring-based capability witness learning scores each branch by its weakest evidence, checks joint support for the extracted requirements within one implementation, and selects the strongest alternative. To reduce the influence of extraction errors, we develop ranking-feedback graph calibration that adjusts unreliable evidence for candidate comparison. Experiments on SkillRet show that SKALOS improves NDCG@10 by 2.68 percentage points over a matched text-only reranker. Witness-guided skill selection also increases ALFWorld task success rate from 22% to 29%.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 SKALOS，一个面向 LLM agent 技能库的图原生重排序器：用多层级能力图对齐语义相近技能的等价表述并保留各自能力证据，以半环式「能力见证」按最弱证据打分并检验单一实现能否联合满足查询要求，再用排序反馈校准不可靠证据。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「按最弱证据打分、检验同一实现内的联合支持」的见证机制，可能与 LVR 中多条视觉或推理证据如何组合并核验共同支撑、避免各自相关却联合不足的问题形成概念类比，可供核查；原文本身面向文本技能检索，不涉及视觉或多模态推理。
